title: ICS Line Parser Stepper
description: The server reads the school calendar as an iCalendar feed, one line at a time. A few rules do most of the work: a line that starts with a space continues the line before it; everything inside a VTIMEZONE block is skipped; a DTSTART with TZID is a local time to convert to UTC; and an all-day DTEND is exclusive, so the last day is one day earlier.

learningObjectives: The learner will execute the iCalendar parsing rules on the 14 lines of a small feed by choosing what the parser does with each line, with at least 12 of the 14 choices correct.
prerequisites: property, parameter, VEVENT, VTIMEZONE, line folding, all-day date, exclusive end date, UTC, TZID (all defined in the section "Step Two: An iCalendar Feed, Parsed on the Server" above this block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Why is the DTSTART on line 2 not an event?
Why is the last day of Thanksgiving Break November 27 and not 28?
Is a time with a TZID already in UTC?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The DTSTART inside a VTIMEZONE is an event. (2) A line that starts with a space is a new property. (3) The end date of an all-day event is its last day. (4) A time with a TZID is already in UTC.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all fourteen lines. Mastery is 12 of 14 correct on the first attempt.
